content.comment_body: I am currently researching Ethernet communication options for a [product_name] PLC. When scanning the network with Wireshark, I observe a TCP stream where elements of the loaded program are visible alongside many blank sections. Does anyone know what higher-level protocol is being used here? Is it similar to the connection established by programming software when communicating with the PLC? Below is an excerpt from the stream I followed: K...........GetHWType....'..K..`.............K...........GetHWId......'..K .`..............K...........CheckState...'..K..`.............K...........CheckState...'..K..`.............K...........GetVersion...'..K .`..............K...........GetPrgHead...'..K..`..................}...J.....Uihu...\Uihu...\Uihu...\Uihu...\K...........CheckState...'..K..`.............K...........HasHoursCnt..'..K..`.............K...........GetAiCnt.....'..K..`.............K...........CheckMS......'..KP.`.................KP..........StartDown....'......];._.K..`............K.0.........InDown.......'................;.E.2LUihu...\Uihu...\Uihu...\Uihu...\...................................
The S7 protocol can be selected in Wireshark, which reveals more details about the communication. However, I haven't used this option myself and can't assist further. Regards, [user_name]

I've attempted to decode the communication using various tools in the past, but found it too time-consuming. Programming the controller without the official software doesn't seem feasible in my experience. The most practical method is to use tools that allow simple status queries for inputs and outputs. Wishing you success in finding a solution! Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The main topic is investigating how the [product_name] PLC communicates via Ethernet, with an emphasis on understanding the protocol beyond the identified TCP streams. While tools like Wireshark can expose some details, the protocol used between the PLC and the programming software is not easy to interpret or reverse-engineer. Other users confirm that advanced communication or programming without official support is significantly restricted and mostly limited to basic status monitoring, due to insufficient public documentation.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for clarity regarding the programming protocol used by the [product_name] PLC, hoping to develop bespoke integrations or alternative programming workflows, similar to how S7 protocol details are accessed on other PLC platforms.
